summary: Old Baldy fire lookout on Mount Wrightson, Santa Cruz County, AZ: built about 1909, final version removed late 1950s; stone foundation remains on the summit.

facts.design: Final 1928 version about 12 by 12 feet, with a cupola holding a fire finder, on a platform 4 feet above ground; earlier lookouts were smaller
facts.status_note: The final lookout was removed in the late 1950s; parts of its stone foundation remain at the summit.

access.note: The summit is reached on foot by trails; the lookout site is the summit foundation.

visit.trail_note: Old Baldy Trail (#372) or the Super Trail to the summit, starting from Mount Wrightson Picnic Area for the Old Baldy route

facts.agency: USDA Forest Service, Coronado National Forest

events.note: First lookout, estimated under six feet square with no windows; used only while a lookout was on duty
Tucson Citizen (as quoted by Forest Lookouts) said a lookout would be kept on Old Baldy, with telephone links to ranger stations
Telephone line from the Madera Administrative Site completed to the lookout
Ranger cabin (Baldy Cabin) built near Baldy Spring for rangers off lookout duty
Slightly larger lookout, about 8 by 8 feet, replaced the first; the Forest Service replaced it

Baldy station said a reported fire in the Huachucas seemed to be only a small building or burning rubbish; reported a fire of fairly large size in Mexico about 30 miles south of Nogales (Tombstone Epitaph, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
About 12 by 12 foot building with a cupola and fire finder replaced the 1920 lookout
Final lookout removed in the late 1950s; by 1958 only the decking with a crawl space remained
Baldy Cabin near Baldy Spring burned in the fall of 1973 and its remnants were removed; this is the cabin, not the lookout
Summary says only parts of the stone foundation remain
Visitor describes the summit as holding the lookout foundation; visit dated February 22, 2022

resolved_conflicts.explanation: GVRHC and the Forest Service give 9,453 feet; Wikipedia gives 9,456 feet. The record has no elevation set, so none was changed.

notes_for_editor: Brief records kind as ground; the 1928 structure was a cabin on a low platform, so the kind looks fair. Only two sources describe the lookout itself (a 2011 GVRHC summary and a 2022 personal blog). The 1911 and 1922 newspaper items come through Forest Lookouts' transcriptions, not the original papers. No staffing fact is recorded: the sources show on-duty use before 1958 and periodic ranger use of the cabin, not a staffing history. Elevation_m is not set. A 1911 item says a lookout 'will be kept' while GVRHC dates the first structure to about 1909; the two are not clearly in conflict.
